topic: Diego Garcia and the Chagos Islands

subtopics.title: Sovereignty Deal and Diego Garcia Base
subtopics.summary: Britain has agreed to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, but the UK will retain sovereign rights over Diego Garcia. A joint UK-US military base there will remain operational for an initial period of 99 years. US concerns centre on strategic autonomy and base security, and Trump criticised the plan.
facts: Britain has agreed to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius.
The Chagos archipelago comprises 58 islands, with Diego Garcia the largest.
The UK retains sovereign rights over Diego Garcia under the agreement.
A joint UK-US military base on Diego Garcia will remain operational for an initial period of 99 years.
Diego Garcia is located in the Central Indian Ocean.
US concern: a sovereignty change may affect strategic autonomy and base security.
Trump criticised the UK plan, citing the strategic importance of the US military base.
The issue is sensitive because it pits decolonisation against security interests.

subtopics.title: Colonial History of the Chagos Islands
subtopics.summary: Portuguese navigators discovered the Chagos Islands in the 16th century, and the islands later came under French control. After Napoleon's defeat, Britain took control of both Chagos and Mauritius, and France ceded the islands to Britain in 1814. Mauritius later argued that it had been coerced into giving up the islands, in violation of UN Resolution 1514.
facts: Portuguese navigators discovered the Chagos Islands in the 16th century.
The Chagos Islands later came under French control.
After Napoleon's defeat, Britain took control of both Chagos and Mauritius.
In 1814, France ceded the islands to Britain.
Mauritius argued that it was coerced into giving up the islands during colonial rule.
UN Resolution 1514 prohibited the breakup of colonies before independence.
The UK claimed that the ICJ had no jurisdiction over the matter.
Mauritius is a former British and French colony that gained independence from British rule in 1968.

subtopics.title: MAHASAGAR and Maritime Initiatives
subtopics.summary: MAHASAGAR is an Indian Navy initiative launched in 2023 that builds on India's 2015 SAGAR maritime doctrine. It widens the focus from India's immediate neighbourhood to the broader Global South, with trade, security, technology and finance as key areas. New tools under it include the IOS Sagar platform and the AIKEYME naval exercise with African nations.
facts: MAHASAGAR builds on India's 2015 Maritime Doctrine, SAGAR.
MAHASAGAR was launched by the Indian Navy in 2023.
MAHASAGAR widens the scope of SAGAR from India's immediate maritime neighbourhood to the broader Global South.
MAHASAGAR's key focus areas are trade for development, mutual security, technology sharing and financial assistance.
MAHASAGAR is a bi-annual initiative that convenes naval chiefs and maritime officials from littoral states.
IOS Sagar uses the INS Sunayna platform to deepen naval cooperation with Indian Ocean littorals.
AIKEYME is a large-scale naval exercise with African nations.
AIKEYME means Unity in Sanskrit, symbolising solidarity with African partners.
